summary: Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi, Robert A. F. Thurman, and postdoctoral mentor Bratindra Nath Mukherjee.

Mircea Eliade (1907–1986) worked in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bucharest and studied at the University of Calcutta. His career included posts at Bucharest, the Sorbonne, and the University of Chicago.
Mireille Helffer (1928–2023) was a Tibetologist and researcher. She served as Chargé de Recherche at the CNRS from circa 1967 to 1993 and held a post at Paris Nanterre University (attested 1985).

Miri Albahari is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD at the University of Calgary under John A. Baker, later holding posts at UNSW and the University of Western Australia.

Miriam Levering (born 1943) works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee (attested 2007–2010).

Mirjan Damaška (born 1931) studied at Zagreb, the Hague Academy, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, and Ljubljana (PhD 1960). He held posts at Zagreb, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, the University of Pennsylvania, and Yale Law School.

Mirle Srinivasa Nagaraja Rao (1932–2011) specialized in Indology and archaeology. Educated at Mysore and Savitribai Phule Pune universities, he held posts at Karnatak University, the Karnataka archaeology department, and served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India.
Mitchell G. Weiss is an Indologist who studied under Ludo Rocher. He has held a post as Professor at the University of Basel.

Mitsuji Fukunaga (1918–2001) was a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religious studies who studied at Hiroshima Higher Normal School and Kyoto University. He held professorships at Kyoto University, the University of Tokyo, Kansai University, and the University of Kitakyushu.
Mitsukuni Yoshida (1921–1991) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University and later held a post at Kyoto University of the Arts from circa 1986 to 1989.

Mitsunobu Nakasone specializes in Buddhist studies. Nakasone has held academic appointments at Bukkyo University as a part-time lecturer (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).
Mitsutoshi Moriguchi (born 1944) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also held a post as a lecturer (attested 1989–1995).

Mitsuyoshi Saegusa (1923–2010) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tokyo, Munich (PhD), and Kokugakuin (PhD). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Kokugakuin, Nihon University, Tsukuba, and the Eastern Institute.

Mitsuyuki Ishida (1911–1991) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He later served on the faculty at Ryukoku University (attested 1956, 1976) and as a professor at International Buddhist University (attested 1976).

Mizuho Okita (born 1977) specializes in Indology and religious studies. Okita completed a BA at Tokai University, studied at Gakushuin University under Atsuhiko Yoshida and Katsuhiko Kamimura, and served as a part-time lecturer at Meisei University.
Mizumaro Ishida (1917–2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Tokai University, an affiliation attested in 1976 and 1987.
Mohammad Ashraf Dar is an Indology and history scholar. He earned a Master of Philosophy degree at Vikram University, where he was also attested as a research scholar in 2014.
Mohammad Habib (1895–1971) was a historian who studied at the University of Allahabad, Aligarh Muslim University, and New College, Oxford, between circa 1916 and 1920.

Mokurai Shimaji (1838–1911) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Chō Sanshū. He held leadership posts at Nishi Hongan-ji, Hongan-ji, and Gankyo-ji, and founded Chiyoda Jogakuen.

Mona Schrempf specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a doctorate in anthropology from the Free University of Berlin (2001) and held posts at the Humboldt University of Berlin and Heidelberg University (attested 2006).
